# Overview: inReach subscription plans


October 20, 2026


### *Find an inReach plan that works for you so you can stay connected when it matters.*


From hiking alpine trails to paddling remote rivers, one thing remains essential to recreators: staying connected when it counts. Since 2011,[Garmin devices with inReach® connectivity](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/c/outdoor-recreation/satellite-communicators/#satellite-messaging-devices) have been trusted tools for those who venture beyond cell service1.


Once you have your inReach device, you must choose a service plan to utilize features like SOS, two-way messaging, live tracking and more. To make this choice easier, we’ve put together a short guide to help you select the best option for your needs.


## Garmin inReach plans


Garmin’s service plans for inReach devices allow you to connect with friends and family beyond the limits of cellular networks. inReach plans enable features like two-way messaging, weather forecasts and live tracking with LTE and satellite connectivity (features vary by device). In an emergency, you can trigger an interactive SOS message with your GPS coordinates to Garmin ResponseSM, our 24/7-staffed international response coordination center.


All plans include emergency SOS messaging. You can move between plans as your needs change or suspend service at no cost.


## Which plan is right for me?


Below are summaries of each plan option (features vary by device). For an overview of features and costs, see[inReach consumer plans.](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/837461/)


**Premium** : Ideal for users who want to be as connected as possible outside of cellular coverage, our top-tier plan includes SOS and unlimited text messages, check-in messages/reactions, weather requests and live tracking/location requests. Fifty photo/voice messages (available only on compatible devices paired with the Garmin Messenger™ app) are included.


**Standard** : For users who need more freedom with their text messaging and who depend on tracking, our second highest plan includes SOS messaging and 150 text messages and weather requests. Check-ins, reactions and tracking features are unlimited. The plan comes with 50 photo/voice messages (available only on compatible devices paired with the Garmin Messenger app) included.


**Essential** : Our middle-tier plan is ideal for users who plan to use text messaging when necessary but don’t expect a lot of back-and-forth communication. It includes SOS messaging and 50 text messages and weather requests. Check-ins and reactions are unlimited, and tracking features are pay-as-you-go. 25 photo/voice messages (available only on compatible devices paired with the Garmin Messenger app) are included.


**Enabled** : This plan is best for users who want basic features and peace of mind. This plan keeps your device active at a low monthly cost and provides a great value, especially for smartwatch customers that prioritize LTE connectivity. It includes SOS messaging and is pay-as-you-go for all other messaging, weather requests and tracking features.


**Suspend** : The[suspend option](https://support.garmin.com/en-US/?faq=n8p5GpSM4128h6i2Sofee6) allows you to pause your inReach plan at no cost for up to 12 months at a time. You can move back into an active plan at any time with no reactivation fee. To maintain[SOS capabilities with a suspended plan](https://support.garmin.com/en-US/?faq=eJz14OUvnG1MivsmEzhSi8) , pair and connect your[compatible device](https://support.garmin.com/en-US/?faq=eJz14OUvnG1MivsmEzhSi8) with the latest software in the[Garmin Messenger app](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/p/893837/) .


## What’s the difference between suspend and cancel?


If you don’t need your inReach device for periods of time, the Suspend option puts your device into a “paused” state with no monthly fees. You can easily switch back to an active plan at no cost anytime. If you cancel and choose to reactivate, you will have to go through the activation process again and will be charged the activation fee.


¹Active plan required. Some jurisdictions regulate or prohibit the use of satellite communication devices; it is the responsibility of the user to know and follow all applicable laws.
